english: Let $C$ be a curve in the first quadrant passing through the point $(1,2)$ such that, for every point $P(x,y)$ on $C$, the normal to $C$ at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at the point $(3x,0)$. If the point $\left(\sqrt{7},\beta\right)$ lies on $C$, then $\beta$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $C$ प्रथम चतुर्थांश में बिन्दु $(1,2)$ से होकर जाने वाला एक वक्र है, जिसके प्रत्येक बिन्दु $P(x,y)$ के लिए $P$ पर $C$ का अभिलम्ब $x$-अक्ष से बिन्दु $(3x,0)$ पर मिलता है। यदि बिन्दु $\left(\sqrt{7},\beta\right)$, $C$ पर स्थित है, तो $\beta$ बराबर है
solution: Normal at $P$: $Y-y=-\dfrac{1}{y'}(X-x)$; with $Y=0$, $X=x+yy'$ (foot of the normal)
solution_full: At $P(x,y)$ the normal is $Y-y=-\dfrac{1}{y'}(X-x)$. Putting $Y=0$: $X=x+yy'$. So the normal meets the $x$-axis at $(x+yy',0)$; the length $yy'$ is the subnormal.
Since $(1,2)$ lies on $C$: $4=2+C$, so $C=2$ and $C$ is the part of $y^{2}=2x^{2}+2$ in the first quadrant.
At $x=\sqrt7$: $y^{2}=14+2=16$, so $\beta=4$ (positive, since $C$ is in the first quadrant).
Option (D) comes from using the tangent instead of the normal or taking $yy'=x$; option (B) from $y^{2}=x^{2}+2$.
originality_note: New: a curve defined by where its normal meets the x-axis, relative to the abscissa of the point. Closest known: curves with constant subnormal (parabolas). Different because: the subnormal grows with x, so the curve is a hyperbola y^2 = 2x^2 + 2.
blueprint_concepts: Geometrical applications: tangent, normal, subtangent, subnormal conditions

concept_use.Geometrical applications: tangent, norma: The foot of the normal on the x-axis is (x + y y', 0), so the condition fixes the subnormal y y' = 2x, which is the differential equation of C.
